abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is a confounding factor that stems from individual cell decisions, regulation among diverse cells, and regulation between these cells and the tumor microenvironment. Identifying cellular and microenvironmental factors that drive tumor heterogeneity is critical to effective therapeutic targeting. However, current experimental methods to uncover the drivers of such heterogeneity can obscure the relative contributions of the microenvironment and cell-intrinsic properties. Similarly, standard parameter estimation methods for spatiotemporal models do not rank parameter importance or resolve equifinality, the property by which different parameter combinations yield equivalent emergent behaviors. Here, we introduce a likelihood-free discovery of emergent drivers pipeline to uncover combinations of parameter distributions that lead to observed emergent tissue dynamics and compare parameter-output dependence among equifinal fitted regions. This pipeline couples approximate Bayesian computation with sequential Monte Carlo and distributed random forests to fit target metrics and characterize these associations within spatiotemporal agent-based models. Mutual information analysis compares these dependence profiles among regions. We leverage correlations among the gen-4 particles to reduce the parameter search space via pairwise linear regression substitution and hierarchical clustering-based grouping without degrading fit to emergent target metrics. When applied to breast cancer data, the pipeline identifies separated fitted parameter regions that reproduce similar target metrics and exhibit different parameter-output dependence profiles. These findings identify candidate parameter relationships for direct tests of mechanistic redundancy.
